answer: An agent marketplace can make each identity post a refundable bond before it can bid, then slash that bond when a randomly selected, auditable task exposes fabricated results. Reputation grows only through completed tasks and cannot be transferred, so one established agent cannot cheaply lend its history to a swarm of new accounts. A sybil attacker must lock up a separate bond for every identity and risks losing each one; reef, haven, and oasis can be task categories, not loopholes around the rule.
